document.title: Transcript of A. N. Kosygin-A.A. Gromyko-D.F. Ustinov-B.N. Ponomarev-N.M. Taraki Conversation on March 20, 1979
document.authors: Soviet leadership (Kosygin, Gromyko, Ustinov, Ponomarev) and Nur Mohammed Taraki
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Conversation between Soviet leaders and Taraki during the Herat crisis, when the Afghan leadership asked for urgent military assistance (over 20 requests in 1979). The Soviets decided on equipment and advisers but no troops.

events.description: Kosygin, Gromyko, Ustinov and Ponomarev meet Taraki in Moscow; Soviets decline to send troops, promise arms and aid.
Military town in Herat retaken by paratroopers backed by tanks after airstrikes.
Zia-ul-Haq statement that Afghanistan events are internal and Pakistan will not interfere.
Soviet resolution on free deliveries of arms, 100,000 tons of wheat and gas price increase.
Kosygin, Gromyko, Ustinov, Ponomarev meet Taraki in Moscow; discuss wheat, loan deferment, radio station, military advisors; Brezhnev meeting to follow.
Taraki to meet Brezhnev 10 minutes after the conversation.
USSR sent 4 MI-8 helicopters to Afghanistan free of charge.
Four more helicopters scheduled to arrive in Afghanistan.
Soviet resolution on military deliveries, wheat and gas prices made known in Kabul the previous evening.
Kosygin, Gromyko, Ustinov, Ponomarev met Taraki in Moscow; Soviet side agreed to political support, arms deliveries, training, and a propaganda specialist.
Brezhnev meeting with Taraki to follow within ten minutes of the Kosygin conversation.
Kosygin, Gromyko, Ustinov and Ponomarev met Taraki in Moscow.
Taraki was scheduled to meet Brezhnev at 18:00-18:30.
Paratroopers supported by tanks, after airstrikes, retook the Herat military town held by the mutinous 17th Infantry Division.
The USSR sent documents to the leaders of Iran and Pakistan warning them against interference in Afghanistan.
After Taraki's radio address on Herat, 102 demonstrations took place across Afghanistan condemning Khomeini.
Zia-ul-Haq statement: Afghan events an internal matter, Pakistan will not interfere, humanitarian aid to refugees conditional.
Pravda article analyzing schemes against the DRA published.
Iranian government ordered foreign workers to leave by April 21 and foreign specialists by June 21.
Kosygin, Gromyko, Ustinov, Ponomarev meet Taraki; discuss helicopters, pilots, officers, wheat.
USSR sent 4 MI-8 helicopters to Afghanistan.
Soviet resolution on large military deliveries, 100 thousand tons of wheat, and gas price increase made known in Kabul the previous evening.

relationships.detail: Kosygin speaks on the Politburo's behalf; the Politburo entrusted the delegation with the talks.
relationships.quote: The Politburo has entrusted us with discussing with you all questions

relationships.detail: Kosygin states the friendship is lasting and promises assistance against all enemies.
relationships.quote: the friendship between Soviet Union and the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan is not conditional, dictated by some temporary viewpoints, but calculated for ages.

relationships.detail: The mutinous section of the 17th infantry division was in the military town in Herat.
relationships.quote: the military town in Herat, the location of the mutinous section of the 17th, infantry division

relationships.detail: Part of the 17th Infantry Division mutinied against the government and was retaken by loyal troops.
relationships.quote: mutinous section of the 17th, infantry division, has been taken by a battalion of paratroopers supported by tanks from Kanilagar

relationships.detail: Herat was described as a center of counter-revolution before the government regained control.
relationships.quote: the city had become a center of counter-revolution.

relationships.detail: Kosygin says Soviet troops entering Afghanistan would vindicate China and other aggressors.
relationships.quote: as soon as our troops cross the border, China and all other aggressors will be vindicated.

relationships.detail: Kosygin cites Vietnam as fighting Chinese aggression without foreign troops.
relationships.quote: are now fighting against Chinese aggression, but no one can accuse the Vietnamese of using foreign troops.

relationships.detail: The USSR sent a document to Iran's leaders warning them not to meddle in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: today we are sending two documents to the leaders of Iran and Pakistan, in which we tell them with all seriousness not to meddle

relationships.detail: The USSR sent a document to Pakistan's leaders warning them not to meddle in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: today we are sending two documents to the leaders of Iran and Pakistan, in which we tell them with all seriousness not to meddle

relationships.detail: Taraki accuses Pakistan's ruling circles of sabotage and subversion against Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: the ruling circles in Pakistan, seeing its revolutionary influence on their people, crossed over to the politics of sabotage and subversive activities against us.

relationships.detail: Taraki says Muslim Brotherhood members who fled after the revolution infiltrated Afghanistan, implying a Pakistani base.
relationships.quote: infiltrated by members of "the Moslem brotherhood" who had fled the country after the revolution

relationships.detail: Taraki describes the Brotherhood as infiltrating and subverting Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: infiltrated by members of "the Moslem brotherhood"

relationships.detail: Taraki visited the USSR and signed an important treaty.
relationships.quote: After my visit to Soviet Union and the signing of a very important Treaty between our countries

relationships.detail: Taraki speaks as leader of the DRA; demonstrators shouted slogans supporting the DRA and Taraki.
relationships.quote: "Long live the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan!" and "Long live Taraki!"

relationships.detail: Taraki says the Treaty signed after his Soviet visit and close friendship with the USSR drive hostility from imperialists.
relationships.quote: It is in the close friendship of Afghanistan and the Soviet Union that one finds the main reason for anti-Afghan activity

relationships.detail: Taraki says Muslim Brotherhood members who fled after the revolution infiltrate Afghanistan, alongside Pakistani-backed subversion.
relationships.quote: infiltrated by members of "the Moslem .brotherhood" who had fled the country after the revolution

relationships.detail: Pakistan's ruling circles adopted sabotage and subversion against the DRA after land reform.
relationships.quote: the ruling circles in Pakistan, seeing its revolutionary influence on their people, crossed over to the politics of sabotage and subversive activities against us

relationships.detail: Taraki says Iran and especially Pakistan don't want friendship with the DRA.
relationships.quote: Iran, and especially . Pakistan don’t want friendship with us.

relationships.detail: Zia issued a statement on Pakistan's non-interference and refugee aid.
relationships.quote: A statement has just been received from Ziafi-ul-Khag, in which he notes that events in Afghanistan are the internal matter of that state

relationships.detail: Taraki alleges Pakistan runs camps training commandos against the DRA under the cover of humanitarian aid for refugees.
relationships.quote: They only speak of humanitarianism, but are themselves creating camps to train commandos against us.

relationships.detail: Ponomarev suggests Zia's statement was Pakistan's reaction to the Pravda article.
relationships.quote: the statement of Ziah-ul-Khaq is Pakistan’s reaction to the story in the newspaper "Pravda."

relationships.detail: Taraki emphasizes lasting friendship and learning from Lenin.
relationships.quote: we have been and will continue to remain friends, and that we shall never be as close to anyone as we are with you

relationships.detail: Taraki names Pakistanis, Iranians, Americans and Chinese as undermining the DRA.
relationships.quote: the Pakistanis, the Iranians, the Americans and the Chinese are undertaking such active steps to undermine us

relationships.detail: Spiritual leaders changed tactics, shouting that Afghanistan had become pro-Soviet and pro-communist.
relationships.quote: the spiritual leaders have changed tactics and have begun to shout that Afghanistan has become pro-Soviet, pro-communist

relationships.detail: At least 200 thousand Afghans work in Iran, having moved 5-6 years earlier under Daoud and before.
relationships.quote: No less than 200 thousand people. They moved to Iran 5-6 years ago, during the regime of Daoud and even earlier.

relationships.detail: Ustinov promises MI-24 armored helicopters: 6 in June-July and 6 more in Q4.
relationships.quote: We will give you.6 such helicopters during June-July and 6 more in the fourth quarter of this year.

relationships.detail: Kosygin offers maintenance specialists but not battle crews or pilots for helicopters.
relationships.quote: We can send you maintenance specialists, which would take care of these helicopters at the airport, but, of course, not battle crews.

relationships.detail: The USSR helped Vietnam extensively but sent only technical specialists, not pilots.
relationships.quote: we have helped and are helping Vietnam a great deal, but they never asked us to send them our pilots.

relationships.detail: The USSR is training 400 Afghan officers; 190 finishing this year, incl. 16 airplane and 13 helicopter pilots.
relationships.quote: We are training 400 Afghan officers.

relationships.detail: Taraki says Afghan officers sent to study in the USSR include many 'Muslim brothers' and Chinese sympathizers; Kosygin offers to send them back.
relationships.quote: there are many "Muslim brothers" and Chinese sympathizers

relationships.detail: Gorelov is chief Soviet military advisor in Afghanistan and will transmit list of graduates.
relationships.quote: through the chief military advisor in Afghanistan general Gorelov, the list of graduates

relationships.quote: during Daoud’s regime, members of the “Muslim Brotherhood" and the pro-Chinese "Shoal-i-Jawid" organizations were sent over to the Soviet Union

key_claims: Soviet leadership explicitly rejects deploying troops to Afghanistan in March 1979, fearing international and domestic backlash.
Taraki blames Pakistan, Iran, the USA and China for subversion, including Muslim Brotherhood infiltrators and training camps.
The USSR pledges free arms, helicopters (Mi-24, Mi-8), wheat and advisors instead of troops.
Taraki says Afghan officers trained in USSR include Muslim Brotherhood and pro-Chinese Shoal-i-Jawid sympathizers.
Zia-ul-Haq publicly states Pakistan will not interfere in Afghanistan, which Kosygin treats as binding but not fully credible.
The Soviet leadership promised the DRA political support and extensive military and other shipments but ruled out invasion or foreign tank and pilot operators.
Taraki requested wheat, loan deferment, a 1000 kW radio station and additional military shipments.
Kosygin said Soviet military specialists would be mechanics, not combat operators, and rejected socialist-country pilots and tank crews as a political problem.
Taraki alleged China was pushing Pakistan against Afghanistan.
Kosygin said the USSR had sent messages to Pakistan's president, Khomeini and Iran's prime minister to deter aggression against Afghanistan.
